title: Tenant Guard: reconcile SSO session replay + KMS unwrap drift causing audit gaps in private clusters
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several enterprise Private customers reported missing or delayed audit entries after bulk SSO re-auth events. Root cause traces to a race between SSO session reconciliation (IdP-initiated rebinds) and our async KMS unwrap worker: when a tenant token is rewrapped during a short window, RBAC lookups use the incoming assertion but the KMS unwrap returns an older envelope and the audit-stream emitter drops the event. This manifests as: 1) action accepted by the runtime, 2) no corresponding audit event in the control plane (gap), 3) intermittent permission denial for follow-up requests using the new assertion. Impact spans VPC private clusters with customer-managed IdPs and recent KMS envelope rotation. The bug is regressional relative to the tenant-claim rehydration changes shipped last quarter.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a private cluster with SAML IdP and scheduled KMS envelope rotation. 2) Trigger IdP-initiated SSO session refresh for 10 concurrent sessions. 3) Simultaneously run kms-wrap to rotate envelopes. 4) Observe control-plane audit logs for missing entries for ~10-20% of the requests. 5) Reproduce locally with federation test harness: ./scripts/fed-test --sessions=10 --wrap-window=200ms
impact_summary: High-severity for customers using Private: gaps in audit trails break compliance controls, SLOs for audit delivery violated, and some tenants see transient RBAC failures leading to customer escalations and an open support ticket per affected org.
mitigation_plan: Short term: deploy an emergency control-plane patch that serializes claim rehydration and KMS unwrap per-tenant key (hotfix) and add a guard that stalls audit emission until envelope version is validated. Rollout as canary to 3 private customers first. Long term: refactor unwrap worker to be idempotent by envelope-versioning and add end-to-end audit watermarks with retry/backpressure. Also add telemetry: metrics for audit-drop-rate per-tenant and unwrap-latency histogram.
implementation_notes: - Minimal hotpatch: add per-tenant mutex in control-plane claim-sync path; verify with unit tests and a short e2e scenario. - Avoid global locks to keep throughput. - Use existing tenant-index shard lock. - Add feature flag tenant_guard.enable_strict_unwrap=true. - Ensure flag defaults to on for private clusters that opted into strict security mode.
risks_and_tradeoffs: - Mutex introduces contention; we mitigate by sharding locks by tenant-id prefix. - Stalling audit emission adds latency to control-plane response; acceptable for private compliance customers but should be limited to canary and behind the feature flag. - Rolling KMS changes may surface related race conditions in dedicated/hosted; test on those planes but do not enable by default.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for unwrap-version check and mutex acquisition. - Integration test using fed-test harness with simulated IdP and KMS rotation. - Canary: deploy to 3 private clusters (small tenants) and run workload generator for 24h. - Post-deploy: monitor metrics: audit-drop-rate, unwrap-latency, control-plane-error-rate. - Regression: run previous customer-repro scripts from support tickets.
deployment_steps: 1) Branch: eng/tenant-guard-unwrap-hotfix. 2) QA: run integration smoke in staging. 3) Merge and build image tagged priv-2026.03.1-hotfix-1. 4) Canary deploy to 3 customers via control-plane rollout config. 5) Monitor 6h, if stable roll to remaining private clusters over 12h. 6) Flip feature flag globally after 72h stable.
